correctness.rationale: A proper color class in K_{n_1,...,n_r} must be contained in one part. Two color classes in different parts induce K_{a,b} and contain the connected bipartite forbidden H exactly when (a,b) dominate its two shore sizes (s,t) in either order. Maximizing per-part classes reduces to exactly two exhaustive regimes: no class of size >=t, or one part allowed large classes while every other part has classes of size <=s-1. The matching lower and upper constructions give chi = sum_i ceil(n_i/(t-1)) for s=1; for s>=2, chi = min{sum_i ceil(n_i/(t-1)), min_j[1+sum_{i!=j}ceil(n_i/(s-1))]}. Boundaries t>=2, r>=2 and n_i>=1 are properly handled; independent partition search checked 270 small tuples, while the two-regime proof covers all parameters.
residual_risks: Disconnected H need not embed with one bipartition orientation; excluded from theorem. The finite check is only corroboration.
